method: Read-only ELF symbol inspection and x86-64 objdump disassembly; no library execution or modification.

verified_findings.finding: generate_seq checks M low 8 bits, K low 9 bits, N low 7 bits for zero. These host sequence constraints differ from get_m=64 and should not be conflated with a single hardware instruction shape.
Symbols expose implementation and wrapper for generate_dequant_q80_packed_in_q4nx_seq. This proves a Q8 dequantization sequence builder exists, not the device MAC precision.
One forward branch executes and waits on xrt::runlist, then starts a separate xrt::run and waits. Other branches issue individual runs.

Container version 2.21.75; eight-column partition starting at zero; MLIR_AIE DPU kernel ID 0x901; opcode/instruction/count followed by five BO arguments. Embedded PDI UUID 975f2a36-5763-4eed-8b10-718b86b81fe5.
verified_findings.limitation: operations_per_cycle=2048 is a metadata declaration, not measured throughput or proof of arithmetic precision. No AIE instructions decoded yet.

interpretation: Investigate larger sequence GEMM tiles and resident multi-operation overlays; tiny-token GEMV timings cannot predict those gains.
Revisit runlist only with explicit context/ABI compatibility evidence: this repository documents a prior XRT 2.25 ERT_CMD_STATE_ABORT probe.
Host ELF disassembly does not establish native INT8 MAC usage; inspect the separate AIE programs in src/xclbins before drawing precision or device throughput conclusions.
